questions.question: When did Nigeria last win the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON)?
questions.explanation:
Nigeria's Super Eagles have won the Africa Cup of Nations three times: in 1980, 1994, and most recently in 2013. In the 2013 final, they beat Burkina Faso 1-0 in South Africa, thanks to a goal from Sunday Mba.

• Option B (1994) is a trap for their second AFCON title.
• Option C (1980) is their first-ever AFCON title.
• Option D (2023) is a trap for the most recent tournament, where Nigeria were runners-up to Ivory Coast.

questions.question: Who between these two players has the most career goals?
questions.explanation:
As of late 2026, Kylian Mbappe has a higher total career goal count than Erling Haaland.

• Mbappe has surpassed 450 career goals (around 453 as of November 2026), having played significantly more matches for club and country.
• Haaland, despite his incredible scoring rate, has around 399 career goals as of November 2026, largely because he is younger and has played fewer professional matches.

While Haaland often scores at a higher goals-per-game ratio, Mbappe's longer career so far gives him the higher total number of goals.

questions.question: Which footballer is this?
questions.explanation:
The player in the image is Ronaldo Nazario (often referred to as Ronaldo or O Fenômeno). He is a legendary Brazilian striker known for his incredible pace, dribbling, and finishing, having played for clubs like Barcelona, Inter Milan, and Real Madrid, and winning two FIFA World Cups with Brazil.

• Option A (Ronaldinho Gaucho) is a fellow Brazilian legend but has a very distinct appearance.
• Option B (Lionel Messi) is the Argentine forward.
• Option C (Cristiano Ronaldo) is the Portuguese forward.

questions.question: Which footballer is this?
questions.explanation:
The player in the image is Jay-Jay Okocha, a Nigerian football legend renowned for his incredible dribbling skills, technique, and flair. He captained the Super Eagles and was famous for his time at clubs like Paris Saint-Germain and Bolton Wanderers.

• Option A (Nwankwo Kanu) is another Nigerian legend who played for Arsenal and Inter Milan.
• Option B (Daniel Amokachi) is a former Nigerian striker known for his time at Everton.
• Option C (Rashidi Yekini) is Nigeria's all-time top scorer, famous for his goal celebration at the 1994 World Cup.

questions.question: In the league phase of the Champions League tournament, if the game ends in a draw after 90 minutes, what happens?
options: They move directly into penalty kicks
The two teams are disqualified from the tournament
questions.explanation:
In the current Champions League format, the league phase replaced the traditional group stage. The scoring system mirrors domestic leagues: teams earn three points for a win and one point for a draw.

If a match is level after 90 minutes plus stoppage time, there is no extra time or penalty shootout. The match is declared a draw, and each team is awarded one point.

• Option B (extra time) and Option C (penalty kicks) apply only to knockout-stage matches that require a winner.
• Option D (disqualification) is completely incorrect for any standard football match.

questions.question: Which football club has won the most UEFA Champions League titles?
questions.explanation:
Real Madrid is the most successful club in the history of the European Cup and UEFA Champions League, having won the competition a record 15 times.

• Option B (AC Milan) is the second most successful club with 7 titles.
• Option C (Bayern Munich) has 6 titles.
• Option D (Liverpool) also has 6 titles.

Because Real Madrid has won the most titles, they have historically played in the most finals and heard the UEFA Champions League anthem the most times.

questions.question: Which football team is the current Champions League title holder as of November 2026?
questions.explanation:
Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) are the current holders of the UEFA Champions League. They secured back-to-back titles by defeating Arsenal 4-3 on penalties (after a 1-1 draw) in the 2026 final held in Budapest[reference:0][reference:1].

• Option A (Real Madrid) is the most successful club in the competition's history but did not win the most recent edition.
• Option B (Manchester City) won the competition in 2023 but were not the 2026 champions.
• Option D (Bayern Munich) are strong contenders but did not claim the 2026 title.

questions.question: What country won the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation:
Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup, defeating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final at MetLife Stadium in New York/New Jersey[reference:0][reference:1]. The decisive goal was scored by Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, securing Spain's second World Cup title[reference:2].

• Option B (Argentina) were the defending champions and finished as runners-up[reference:4].
• Option C (France) and Option D (Brazil) are traditional powerhouses but did not win the 2026 tournament.

questions.question: According to the Laws of the Game, a player is in an offside position if they are nearer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent at the moment the ball is played. Which of the following is an exception where a player CANNOT be offside?
options: Receiving the ball directly from a throw-in
Receiving the ball from a teammate's deliberate header
Receiving the ball in their own half
Receiving the ball from a teammate's backheel pass
questions.explanation:
A player cannot be offside directly from a throw-in, a goal kick, or a corner kick.

• Option B is incorrect; a player can be offside from a header.
• Option C is technically true that you cannot be offside in your own half, but the question asks for the specific restart exceptions. Option A is the standard technical exception.
• Option D is incorrect; backheel passes are normal open play.

questions.question: How many substitutions are teams currently allowed to make in a standard competitive match?
questions.explanation:
Under current IFAB rules, teams are allowed to make up to 5 substitutions, using a maximum of three stoppages in play (plus half-time) to make them.

• Option A (3) was the old rule before the COVID-19 pandemic.
• Options B and D are incorrect.

questions.question: If an attacking player is fouled inside the penalty area, what is the correct restart?
options: Direct free kick outside the box
Indirect free kick inside the box
questions.explanation:
If a defending player commits a penal offense (like tripping or pushing) against an attacker inside the penalty area, the referee awards a penalty kick.

• Option A would be for a foul outside the box.
• Option C is for non-penal offenses, like a back-pass to the keeper.

questions.question: In football terminology, what does a 'Double Pivot' refer to?
options: Two central midfielders sitting deep together
A fullback and a winger overlapping each other
questions.explanation:
A Double Pivot refers to a tactical setup using two holding (defensive) midfielders playing side-by-side in front of the defense (e.g., a 4-2-3-1 formation). It provides defensive stability and allows the fullbacks to push forward.

• Option A is a strike partnership.
• Option C is double marking.
• Option D is an overlap.

questions.question: How many players are on the field for one football team during a standard match?
questions.explanation:
A standard football team consists of 11 players on the field. This includes 10 outfield players and 1 goalkeeper.

• Option A (9) is incorrect.
• Option B (10) is incorrect.
• Option D (12) is incorrect.

questions.question: A standard football match is divided into two halves. How long is each half?
questions.explanation:
A standard senior football match lasts for 90 minutes in total, divided into two halves of 45 minutes each, plus injury time.

• Option A (30 minutes) is usually for younger age groups.
• Option C (60 minutes) is the length of the whole game in some youth leagues.
• Option D (90 minutes) is the total duration of the match, not one half.

questions.question: Which player on the field is legally allowed to touch the ball with their hands and arms?
questions.explanation:
In football, only the Goalkeeper is allowed to handle the ball with their hands, and they can only do so inside their own penalty area.

• Outfield players (Strikers, Defenders, Midfielders) are not allowed to touch the ball with their hands or arms during open play.

questions.question: What card does a referee show to a player to send them off the pitch permanently?
questions.explanation:
A Red card means a player is sent off the pitch and cannot be replaced. They must leave the field immediately.

• Option A (Yellow card) is a warning for bad behavior or fouls.
• Green and Blue cards are not standard in football.

questions.question: When a single player scores three goals in one match, what is it called?
questions.explanation:
Scoring three goals in a single match is known as a Hat-trick.

• Option C (Treble) usually refers to a team winning three major trophies in one season.

questions.question: What is the restart of play called when the ball goes out of bounds over the long sides of the pitch?
questions.explanation:
When the ball crosses the touchline (the long sides of the pitch), play restarts with a Throw-in.

• Option A (Corner kick) happens when the ball crosses the goal line last touched by a defender.
• Option B (Goal kick) happens when the ball crosses the goal line last touched by an attacker.

questions.question: Which piece of protective equipment is a football player required to wear on their legs?
questions.explanation:
It is a mandatory safety rule in football that all players wear Shin guards to protect their lower legs from kicks and tackles.

• Knee pads and thigh pads are used in other sports.

questions.question: During a free kick, what is the minimum distance the defending players must stand from the ball?
questions.explanation:
Defending players must retreat at least 10 yards (about 9.15 meters) away from the ball for a standard free kick.

• Option C (12 yards) is the distance for a penalty kick.

questions.question: A goal is officially scored when the whole ball crosses which line?
questions.explanation:
For a goal to count, the entire ball must cross the Goal line between the goalposts and under the crossbar.

• The touchline is the side boundary.
• The halfway line divides the pitch in two.

questions.question: What is the name of the large rectangular area in front of the goal where the goalkeeper is allowed to use their hands?
questions.explanation:
The goalkeeper is allowed to handle the ball only within their own Penalty Area (also known as the 18-yard box).

• The Center Circle is where kick-offs happen.
• The Technical Area is where the coaches sit.

questions.question: How is a football match officially started at the beginning of each half?
questions.explanation:
Every football match begins with a Kick-off from the center circle. It is also used to restart the match at the beginning of the second half and after a goal is scored.

• Option A (Throw-in) is used when the ball goes out of bounds on the sides.
• Option B (Corner Kick) is used for corners.
• Option D (Free Kick) is used after a foul.

questions.question: If the attacking team kicks the ball out of bounds over the opponent's goal line (missing the goal), how is play restarted?
questions.explanation:
When the attacking team is the last to touch the ball before it crosses the goal line without a goal being scored, the defending team restarts with a Goal Kick.

• Option A (Corner Kick) happens if the *defending* team kicks it over their own goal line.
• Option C (Throw-in) is only for the long sides of the pitch.

questions.question: What is the distance of the penalty spot from the goal line?
questions.explanation:
The penalty spot is exactly 12 yards (about 11 meters) from the center of the goal line.

• Option A (10 yards) is the distance defenders must stand from a free kick.
• Option D (18 yards) is the distance from the goal line to the edge of the penalty box.

questions.question: In a league tournament, how many points is a team awarded for winning a match?
questions.explanation:
A win in a standard football league earns a team 3 points. A draw earns 1 point, and a loss earns 0 points.

• This system was introduced to encourage teams to attack and play for a win rather than settling for a draw.

questions.question: Which of the following body parts is an outfield player NOT allowed to use to control or pass the ball?
questions.explanation:
Outfield players are strictly prohibited from using their hands or arms to touch the ball during play. If they do, it is a handball offense.

• Players *are* allowed to use their head (Option A), chest (Option B), and thighs (Option C) to control or pass the ball.

questions.question: What is the name of the worldwide governing body for football?
questions.explanation:
FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) is the international governing body responsible for the laws of the game and organizing the World Cup.

• Option A (UEFA) governs football in Europe.
• Option C (CAF) governs football in Africa.
• Option D (IOC) is the International Olympic Committee.

questions.question: How long is the half-time break in a standard professional football match?
questions.explanation:
The half-time interval is typically 15 minutes long, allowing players to rest and receive tactical instructions from their coaches.

• Option B (10 minutes) is common in some youth matches, but 15 is the standard for professional games.

questions.question: If a player receives two yellow cards in the same match, what happens next?
options: They are sent off with a red card
They must sit out for 10 minutes
questions.explanation:
If a player receives a second yellow card in the same match, it is automatically upgraded to a red card. The player is sent off, and their team must play with one fewer player.

• A single yellow card (Option A) is just a warning.

questions.question: What is the term for when a defending player accidentally kicks the ball into their own team's goal?
questions.explanation:
When a player accidentally scores in their own team's net, it is called an Own Goal. The goal is awarded to the opposing team.

• Option A (Hat-trick) is scoring 3 goals for the *other* team.
• Option C (Clean Sheet) means conceding zero goals in a match.

questions.question: What is the name of the line that divides the football pitch into two equal halves?
questions.explanation:
The Halfway Line runs across the middle of the pitch, dividing it into two halves. Kick-offs are taken from the center circle located on this line.

• Option A (Touchline) is the side boundary.
• Option B (Goal line) is the boundary where goals are located.

questions.question: What is it called when a player scores two goals in a single match?
questions.explanation:
Scoring two goals in a single match is known as a Brace.

• Option A (Hat-trick) is scoring three goals.
• Options C and D are not standard football terminology for scoring two goals.

questions.question: What is the maximum amount of time added for extra time in a knockout match?
questions.explanation:
If a match requires a winner and is tied after 90 minutes, extra time is played. It consists of two halves of 15 minutes each, totaling 30 minutes.

• Option A and B are less than standard extra time.
• Option D (45 minutes) is the length of a regular half.

questions.question: What does the term 'Clean Sheet' mean in football?
options: Scoring a goal directly from a corner
A match ending in a draw
questions.explanation:
A Clean Sheet is a term used when a team (specifically the goalkeeper and defense) does not concede any goals during the entire match.

• Options A, C, and D are unrelated to the term.

questions.question: Which official is primarily responsible for enforcing the rules and managing the match on the pitch?
questions.explanation:
The Referee is the main official in charge of the match. They enforce the Laws of the Game, keep time, and make final decisions on fouls and goals.

• The Linesman (Assistant Referee) helps with offsides and out-of-bounds.
• The Fourth Official manages substitutions and the technical area.

questions.question: What is the primary international competition for national men's football teams called?
questions.explanation:
The FIFA World Cup is the highest-level international competition for national teams, held every four years.

• Option A is for European club teams.
• Option C is for African national teams.
• Option D is a domestic league in England.

questions.question: How many minutes are usually added to the end of a half for injuries, substitutions, and time-wasting?
questions.explanation:
Time added by the referee at the end of a half to make up for lost time is called Stoppage time (or injury time).

• Option B is the break between halves.
• Option C is the two 15-minute periods played in knockouts.
• Option D is a historical rule no longer used.

questions.question: What is the name of the official match ball used in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation:
The official match ball for the 2026 FIFA World Cup is named Trionda, designed by Adidas[reference:0][reference:1].

• Option A (Al Rihla) was the official ball for the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.
• Option C (Telstar 18) was the official ball for the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.
• Option D (Jabulani) was the official ball for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa.

questions.question: Who won the Men's Ballon d'Or in 2026?
questions.explanation:
Harry Kane won the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

• Option A (Erling Haaland) and Option B (Kylian Mbappe) were among the top contenders but finished behind Kane in the rankings.
• Option D (Lionel Messi) is an eight-time winner but did not win the 2026 award.
